questions.q: What is the real, key difference between ERC-721's `_owners` mapping and ERC-20's balance mapping?
options: ERC-721 tracks which specific tokenId belongs to which owner; ERC-20 just tracks a plain interchangeable amount per address
They are functionally identical with no real difference
ERC-721 uses arrays instead of mappings entirely
ERC-20 tracks individual token IDs too
questions.explain: Because NFTs are unique, ERC-721 needs a mapping from a specific tokenId to its owner — ERC-20 only ever needed a mapping from address to a fungible amount.

questions.q: Why does `ownerOf` check that the returned owner isn't `address(0)`?
options: Because an unset mapping entry defaults to address(0), which means that token doesn't actually exist yet
Because address(0) always represents the contract's own deployer
Because every valid token must be owned by address(0)
This check has no real purpose
questions.explain: If a tokenId was never minted, its entry in _owners defaults to address(0) — checking for this is how ownerOf detects a nonexistent token.

questions.q: What real, hard rule does `mint` enforce about token IDs?
options: A tokenId that already exists (already has a non-zero owner) cannot be minted again
Token IDs can be reused freely by anyone
Only even-numbered token IDs are valid
Token IDs must always start at zero
questions.explain: mint requires _owners[tokenId] == address(0) — meaning that ID hasn't been claimed yet — since duplicate token IDs would break the uniqueness NFTs depend on.

questions.q: What three real state changes does a successful call to `mint` actually make?
options: It sets the token's owner, increments that owner's balance, and increases totalSupply
It only increments totalSupply, leaving ownership unset
It deletes the recipient's existing balance
It only emits an event with no real state changes
questions.explain: mint assigns _owners[tokenId] = to, increments _balances[to], and increases totalSupply — three real, necessary updates.

questions.q: What does the Transfer event's `from` parameter equal when a brand-new NFT is minted?
options: address(0), since the token had no previous owner
The contract's own address
The token's new owner
It's left blank entirely
questions.explain: Just like with ERC-20 minting, address(0) stands in for "no real previous owner" since the token is being created, not transferred from an existing holder.
